name: main
prose: Program entry of the nc (netcat) utility, main(int argc, char *argv[]), defined at netcat.c:157; it ends the process through exit() or through err/errx/usage, and its end (line 594) is exit(ret) rather than a return. Local ret starts at 1. It ignores SIGPIPE and parses options with getopt_long; bad option values, unsupported combinations (e.g. -l with -s, -p or -z, -k or --lb without -l, --sctp with -u or -U, --tun without -u, proxy with -u/-l/-U/IPv6/-s) and a failed tun open end the process with errx(1,...), and a missing or wrong number of host/port arguments calls usage(1); option h calls help(), which calls usage(0). Option x does strdup of the proxy string, which is not freed anywhere in main. For unix-domain datagram connect it picks the temporary socket path (-s value or a mktemp name). Listen mode (-l) sets ret = 0, creates the unix socket (or calls local_listen each loop for non-unix), and exits with err(1) on listen, recvfrom, connect or accept errors; it then serves the connection (UDP with -k just readwrite, UDP without -k peeks the peer with recvfrom, connects, readwrite; TCP accepts then readwrite and close), closes s for non-unix, and repeats only if -k is set; otherwise falls to the final cleanup. Unix connect mode (non-listen, -U) sets ret = 0 and calls unix_connect; if it returns a value > 0 and -z is not set it does readwrite and close, otherwise ret = 1; it then unlinks the temporary socket if -u and calls exit(ret) directly, without closing tun_fd. Otherwise (inet connect mode) it builds the port list and for each port closes any previous s if nonzero, connects directly or via socks_connect, skips to the next port if the connect fails (s < 0) without changing ret, sets ret = 0 on a connected port, and with -v or -z (for UDP a failed udptest sets ret = 1 and continues) prints the 'succeeded' message, then does fdpass with -F or readwrite unless -z. After the loop the shared tail closes s if nonzero (so listen mode may close an already closed s) and closes tun_fd if open, then exit(ret): ret is 1 if no port got past the connect check, otherwise the value set by the last port that did (0 or 1 from udptest).

name: jsmn_parse
prose: jsmn_parse(parser, js, len, tokens, num_tokens) scans js from parser->pos while pos < len and js[pos] is not NUL, and returns the count of tokens seen (a jsmnerr_t used as int count) or a negative error. It dispatches per character: '{' and '[' increment count and, only if tokens is non-NULL, allocate a token via jsmn_alloc_token (NULL result returns JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM), bump the parent's size, set type/start and make it the current super token. '}' and ']' do nothing when tokens is NULL; otherwise they search back for the innermost open token (start set, end unset), return JSMN_ERROR_INVAL if its type does not match or (in the non-JSMN_PARENT_LINKS build) if no open token exists, and set its end and the new super token. '"' calls jsmn_parse_string and ':' sets toksuper to the last token. ',' with tokens non-NULL moves toksuper back to the enclosing array or object. Whitespace is skipped. Under JSMN_STRICT, a digit, '-', 't', 'f' or 'n' returns JSMN_ERROR_INVAL if tokens is non-NULL and the current super token is an object or a string that already has size; other unexpected characters return JSMN_ERROR_INVAL; without JSMN_STRICT any other character is treated as a primitive. Strings and primitives each count++ and bump the super token's size if tokens is non-NULL; any negative result from jsmn_parse_string or jsmn_parse_primitive is returned unchanged (their bodies were not read, so which codes they produce is not stated here). After the loop, if tokens is non-NULL and any token has start set but end unset, JSMN_ERROR_PART is returned; otherwise count is returned. On an early error return parser->pos is left at the current character (not advanced) and toknext/toksuper as modified so far; the function takes no locks and does not free anything.

name: isc_log_doit
prose: Static function isc_log_doit(lctx, category, module, level, write_once, msgcat, msgset, msg, format, args), defined at log.c:1404-1767, formats and writes one log message. Precondition macros (REQUIRE) assert lctx NULL or valid, category, module and format non-NULL, level != ISC_LOG_DYNAMIC, and (once lctx is non-NULL) category->id and module->id are below the context's counts. It returns with no effect, before taking any lock, if lctx is NULL or isc_log_wouldlog(lctx, level) is false. Otherwise it translates the format through isc_msgcat_get if msgcat is non-NULL, takes lctx->lock, clears lctx->buffer and walks the category's channel list (falling back to the list for category 0, then to the built-in default_channel, when nothing matched). Entries whose module differs from module are skipped; for a matched entry, channels are skipped when DEBUGONLY is set with debug_level 0 or when the channel level is below the message level (dynamic channels compare against lctx->debug_level). For each passing channel it prepares the time and level strings on demand; if lctx->buffer is still empty it formats the message with vsnprintf once, and when write_once is set it first discards history entries older than the duplicate interval, returns with the lock released if the same text is still in the history, and otherwise appends a copy to the history when isc_mem_get succeeds. It then writes to the channel by type: file (reopens or closes when the max size was reached according to the roll settings, may skip the write when the file is still at max size with roll-never, opens the file via isc_log_open and skips the write if that fails) falling through to file-descriptor output with fprintf/fflush and a max-size check, syslog with a mapped syslog level, or null (nothing). It releases lctx->lock at line 1766 or at the early duplicate-return at 1614; no other path after the lock was read to return. Returns void.

name: format_errmsg
prose: format_errmsg(nfmt, lennfmt, fmt, errval), msyslog.c:49-87, copies fmt into nfmt while expanding %m, and returns nothing. It loops while the next fmt character is not NUL and the write pointer n is below nfmt + lennfmt - 1. A character other than '%' is copied. A '%' followed by a character other than 'm' writes '%' and then that character (two bytes, the second skipped if the character is NUL, in which case the loop breaks). '%m' calls errno_to_str(errval, errmsg, 256) into a local 256-byte buffer and copies the text only if n + strlen(text) < nfmt + lennfmt - 1; otherwise the expansion is silently omitted (and the %m is consumed). After the loop it always writes a NUL at *n. The loop condition allows the two-byte '%x' case to start with n at nfmt+lennfmt-2, which leaves n at nfmt+lennfmt, so the final NUL write can land at nfmt[lennfmt], one byte past a buffer of lennfmt bytes; for lennfmt == 0 the final NUL write is at nfmt[0], also outside the buffer. In other cases the result is NUL terminated within lennfmt bytes. No locks or memory are acquired.

name: ntpcal_leapyears_in_years
prose: ntpcal_leapyears_in_years(years) takes an int32_t number of elapsed years and returns an int32_t count of leap years using the 4/100/400 rule. It takes sf32 = int32_sflag(years) (the sign mask, used to flip all bits for negative input), forms uyear = (uint32_t)years ^ sf32 (so uyear = years for years >= 0 and -years-1 for years < 0), computes sum = uyear/4 - uyear/100 + uyear/400 by chained division, and returns uint32_2cpl_to_int32(sf32 ^ sum). For years >= 0 the result is years/4 - years/100 + years/400. For years < 0 the result is the one's complement of that sum for uyear = -years-1, that is -1 - (u/4 - u/100 + u/400) with u = -years-1 (for example years = -1 gives -1). Pure arithmetic on its argument; no locks, memory or globals are touched.

name: fmtflt
prose: Static function fmtflt(str, len, size, fvalue, width, precision, flags, overflow) at snprintf.c:1091-1378 appends a formatted floating-point conversion to str through OUTCHAR, returning nothing. (The sign and thousands-separator settings are not parameters: sign is derived from fvalue and the PLUS/SPACE flags, and separators from flags & PRINT_F_QUOTE.) A precision of -1 becomes 6. If fvalue is NaN or infinite it builds the sign plus "nan"/"inf" (uppercase with PRINT_F_UP) in iconvert, passes it to fmtstr with the width and flags, and returns. For E and G conversions it computes the decimal exponent; precision is capped at 9, 19 or 38 depending on sizeof(UINTMAX_T). If cast(ufvalue) of the scaled magnitude equals UINTMAX_MAX it sets *overflow = 1 and returns without appending anything. Otherwise it rounds the fractional part (carrying into the integer part, and into the exponent in e-style), re-runs the computation in f-style via goto again for %g when the exponent is in range, then outputs, in order: padding (spaces on the left, zeros after the sign when ZERO is set, spaces on the right for MINUS), the sign, the integer digits with grouping separators when requested, the decimal point (locale decimal point if available, else '.'), leading fractional zeros, the fractional digits (minus omitted trailing zeros for %g), and the exponent characters. OUTCHAR always increments *len but stores a character only while *len + 1 < size, so *len can exceed size and the buffer keeps room for a NUL. *overflow is assigned only in the UINTMAX_MAX case.

prose: Static input handler gps_input(parseio, ch, tstamp), clk_meinberg.c:593-733, consumes one received byte for the Meinberg GPS framing state machine kept in the msg_buf stored at parseio->parse_pdata. Returns PARSE_INP_SKIP at once if parse_pdata is NULL. In phase MBG_NONE: SOH sets len = sizeof(header) and phase MBG_HEADER; STX sets len 0, phase MBG_STRING and stores ch as parse_data[0] with parse_index 1; any other byte returns PARSE_INP_SKIP leaving everything unchanged; for SOH/STX it also resets parse_dtime.parse_msglen to 1, stores ch in parse_msg[0], copies *tstamp to parse_stime and returns PARSE_INP_SKIP. In the other phases it appends ch to parse_data when in MBG_STRING and parse_index < parse_dsize, and appends ch to parse_dtime.parse_msg; if parse_msglen then exceeds sizeof(parse_msg) it sets phase MBG_NONE, NUL-terminates parse_data at parse_index, copies index+1 bytes to parse_ldata, sets parse_ldsize = parse_index and returns PARSE_INP_DATA. In MBG_HEADER or MBG_DATA it decrements len and returns PARSE_INP_SKIP while len is nonzero. In MBG_STRING it returns PARSE_INP_TIME (phase back to MBG_NONE, string NUL-terminated and copied to parse_ldata, parse_ldsize set, parse_index reset to 0) when ch is ETX or parse_index >= parse_dsize, otherwise PARSE_INP_SKIP. When the header (len bytes) is complete it decodes it, computes mbg_csum over 6 bytes and compares with header.hdr_csum: a mismatch sets phase MBG_NONE and returns PARSE_INP_DATA without copying to parse_ldata; header.len == 0 sets phase MBG_NONE and returns PARSE_INP_DATA; header.len >= sizeof(parse_msg) - sizeof(header) - 1 sets MBG_NONE and returns PARSE_INP_SKIP (message discarded); otherwise len = header.len, phase MBG_DATA, return PARSE_INP_SKIP. When the data part completes (MBG_DATA with len reaching 0) it sets phase MBG_NONE and returns PARSE_INP_DATA, again without copying to parse_ldata. No locks or allocation.

name: Strncmp
prose: Static function Strncmp(s, t, n) in parsestreams.c:173-191 compares up to n characters of two C strings with an int result. It returns 0 immediately if s or t is NULL or s == t. Otherwise it runs while (n-- && !(c = *s++ - *t++) && *s && *t): the loop stops when n reaches 0 (n == 0 compares nothing and returns 0; a negative n is nonzero, so the count never stops the loop), when a character pair differs (then c, the difference of the two chars, is returned, negative if the s character is smaller), or after an equal pair when either next character is NUL; in that last case c is 0, so the function returns 0 for strings where one is a proper prefix of the other (e.g. "ab" against "abc"), and also returns 0 when both strings end together. An empty string against a nonempty one returns the nonzero difference of the first characters. Note that after an equal pair of NUL characters the loop reads *s and *t one byte past the terminators (the post-increment at 187 runs before the *s && *t test), so for two distinct empty strings and n > 0 the strings must have a readable byte after the NUL. No memory is allocated or freed.

name: zs_xsisr
prose: Static function zs_xsisr(zs), parsestreams.c:1126-1323 (built under sun), is the external-status interrupt handler installed in place of the original one by init_zs_linemon (line 1064). It reads the ZSCC control (status) register. If the carrier-detect bit differs from the saved za_rr0 it stores the new CD bit in za_rr0, timestamps with uniqtime (and with PPS_SYNC, calls hardpps when the logical CD state, honouring cd_invert, is asserted), then walks the read-queue chain from za->za_ttycommon.t_readq looking for the parse module by comparing module id names with Strcmp. If found, it calls parse_iodone only when the stream has PARSE_ENABLE set and parse_iopps(..., SYNC_ONE/SYNC_ZERO, &cdevent) returns nonzero, and when the logical state is asserted it stores the timestamp in parse_ppsclockev and increments its serial; then it stops walking. Reaching the end of the chain without a match is silent; only if the walk goes past MAXDEPTH queues does it call panic. After the CD handling, if no status bit other than CD differs from za_rr0 it writes ZSWR0_RESET_STATUS to the control register and returns 0. Otherwise (and also when CD did not change) it sets or clears ZAS_CARR_ON in za_flags from the current CD bit and walks the chain again: if the parse stream is found it calls the saved original zsop_xsint handler and returns that handler's result, or panics if the saved handler pointer is NULL; if the walk runs past MAXDEPTH it panics; if the chain ends without a match it prints an emergency message and calls the global emergencyzs->zsop_xsint(zs) if present (else panics) and returns 0. It therefore returns 0 on the paths above except where it returns the original handler's result.

name: crypto_xmit
prose: crypto_xmit(peer, xpkt, rbufp, start, ep, cookie), ntp_crypto.c:1082-1407, builds one extension field in the transmit packet at byte offset start and returns an int length, not an XEVNT code. It sets the header at xpkt + start/4 to opcode (upper 16 bits of ep->opcode with length 8) and ep->associd, remembers peer->opcode when peer is non-NULL and the request is not a response, and sets len = 8, rval = XEVNT_OK. It then switches on the upper 16 bits of the opcode: association, certificate, sign, cookie, auto-key and leap requests/responses mostly call crypto_send with the corresponding stored value (CRYPTO_ASSOC also sets fp->fstamp from crypto_flags; CRYPTO_SIGN yields XEVNT_PER if the current time is outside the host certificate's first/last interval; CRYPTO_CERT|RESP yields XEVNT_LEN if the subject name length is 0 or does not fit the 64..-byte certname buffer, otherwise searches cinfo for a non-private, non-error certificate with that subject and sends it, and sends nothing (len stays 8, rval XEVNT_OK) if none matches or crypto_time() is zero); the IFF, GQ and MV requests do nothing when peer is NULL and otherwise call crypto_alice / crypto_alice2 / crypto_alice3, and their responses call crypto_bob / crypto_bob2 / crypto_bob3, sending the result and calling value_free only when the callee returned XEVNT_OK (otherwise rval is that error code); SIGN|RESP uses cert_sign; COOK|RESP checks the value length (XEVNT_LEN on failure) and sends crypto_encrypt output; AUTO|RESP with peer NULL looks the peer up by association id (XEVNT_ERR if not found) and clears FLAG_ASSOC; unknown opcodes give XEVNT_ERR only if the RESP bit is set. If rval is not XEVNT_OK it sets CRYPTO_ERROR in the header opcode, records crypto stats, and returns 0 when the request was not a response; for a response with an error it falls through and returns len (8, or whatever crypto_send had set). Otherwise it returns len, the number of bytes added (8 when no payload was appended). It writes only into xpkt and calls allocation-owning helpers whose bodies were not read.

Reviewer 'original' RIGHT (peer NULL or certificate not found leaves the 8-byte header only, lines 1239, 1226-1230); reviewer round 15 RIGHT (crypto_send appends payload beyond the 8-byte header, so the caller must supply more space). The previous prose said the function returns rval, which is wrong: it returns len (lines 1402 and 1406). crypto_send, crypto_alice* and crypto_bob* not read; the exact certname size is MAXHOSTNAME + 1 (line 1097).

name: crypto_recv
prose: crypto_recv(peer, rbufp), ntp_crypto.c:419-1062, walks the extension fields of a received NTP packet and returns an XEVNT_* code (int). It loops while the bytes remaining after authlen (starting at LEN_PKT_NOMAC) exceed MAX_MAC_LEN; for each field it sets rval = XEVNT_OK, reads opcode and length, and if the crypto version is not CRYPTO_VN or len < 8 it bumps sys_badlength and sets CRYPTO_ERROR in the code (which then falls to the default case and gives XEVNT_ERR). It returns XEVNT_LEN at once if len exceeds the remaining bytes, or if len >= VALUE_LEN and vallen is 0 or does not fit in the field. It then switches on the opcode: ASSOC request (XEVNT_ERR if peer already has CRYPTO_FLAG_CERT, or if peer->cmmd is set and peer->assoc differs from the field's association id; otherwise replaces peer->cmmd with a copy of the field); ASSOC response (leaves everything unchanged with rval XEVNT_OK if peer->crypto is already set and the association ids agree, XEVNT_ERR if they differ; XEVNT_LEN for a bad value length; XEVNT_KEY on private-key or host/flag-mask mismatch; XEVNT_MD for an unknown digest; otherwise stores assoc, crypto flags, digest, a random hcookie, and new subject and issuer strings, freeing the old ones); CERT response (a field shorter than VALUE_LEN only breaks, still XEVNT_OK; otherwise crypto_verify, cert_install (XEVNT_CRT on NULL) and cert_hike errors are returned, and peer->pkey is taken from the certificate if unset); IFF, GQ and MV responses (crypto_verify then crypto_iff/gq/mv; on success set CRYPTO_FLAG_VRFY); COOK response (crypto_verify, then RSA decrypt of the cookie when vallen equals the host key size; allocation failure, decrypt failure or wrong size give XEVNT_CKY; on success it sets peer->pcookie and CRYPTO_FLAG_COOK); AUTO response (crypto_verify, then breaks with rval still XEVNT_OK, without changes, if a broadcast-client association id differs or ep->tstamp is 0; otherwise installs peer->recval and sets CRYPTO_FLAG_AUTO); SIGN response (crypto_verify, cert_install, XEVNT_CRT on failure, sets CRYPTO_FLAG_SIGN); LEAP response (crypto_verify error is returned, a value length other than 3*sizeof(uint32_t) breaks with XEVNT_OK and no change, else updates tai_leap, calls crypto_update and sets CRYPTO_FLAG_LEAP). Request opcodes CERT/IFF/GQ/MV/COOK/SIGN return XEVNT_LEN if len < VALUE_LEN and otherwise, like any other unrecognised request, are queued by copying the field into peer->cmmd if it is NULL; a response or error opcode that is not handled gives XEVNT_ERR. After each field, if rval is not XEVNT_OK it records crypto stats and returns rval at once; otherwise authlen advances by the field length rounded up to 4 bytes. After the loop it returns rval (XEVNT_OK if every field was accepted or there were none). In the COOK path the RSA object from EVP_PKEY_get1_RSA is freed only on the success path; the malloc-failure and decrypt-failure breaks skip RSA_free, while the cookie buffer is freed on those paths. No locks are taken.

name: io_multicast_add
prose: io_multicast_add(addr), ntp_io.c:2781-2882, returns void and does not modify or free *addr. Without MCAST it only logs "Can not add multicast address %s: no multicast support". With MCAST it returns at once, no log, if addr is not a multicast address or find_flagged_addr_in_list(addr, INT_MCASTOPEN) finds an entry. In the default build (MULTICAST_NONEWSOCKET not defined) it creates a new endpoint with new_interface(NULL), copies addr into ep->sin with port NTP_PORT, sets family and an all-ones mask, sets reuseaddr, and calls open_socket. If the socket opens, the endpoint gets ignore_packets false, INT_MCASTIF, ifindex SCOPE(addr), the name "multicast", and is registered with add_interface and logged with log_listen_address. If opening fails it deletes the new endpoint and selects wildipv4 or wildipv6 by the family of addr (ep becomes NULL if neither): when found it stores *addr in that wildcard endpoint's bcast and logs an error, otherwise it logs "No multicast socket available" and returns without adding anything to the address list. In either of the two successful cases it then sets one_ep = ep, calls socket_multicast_enable(ep, addr) exactly once on that endpoint (new or wildcard), logs "Joined ..." if it returns nonzero, and finally calls add_addr_to_list(addr, one_ep). In the MULTICAST_NONEWSOCKET build it sets one_ep to wildipv4 (for an IPv4 addr) or else wildipv6, then loops over ep_list, skipping endpoints that are ignored, of a different address family, lack INT_MULTICAST or have INT_LOOPBACK or INT_WILDCARD; for each remaining endpoint it sets one_ep to it, calls socket_multicast_enable(ep, addr) and logs "Joined ..." on nonzero; then calls add_addr_to_list(addr, one_ep), so one_ep is the last eligible endpoint, or the wildcard endpoint if none was eligible. No locks are taken in this function.

The old prose said socket_multicast_enable is only called in the NONEWSOCKET build, and on the wildcard endpoint as well as the others; in the default build it is called once at 2868 on the new or wildcard endpoint, and in the NONEWSOCKET build only on eligible list entries. name: leapsec_add
prose: Static function leapsec_add(pt, now64, insert), ntp_leapsec.c:930-974, returns a boolean int. It returns FALSE with errno = ERANGE if *now64 is earlier than pt->head.expire (equal to expire passes this test) or if the table is non-empty and *now64 is not later than pt->info[0].ttime (equal is rejected). It converts *now64 to calendar fields and returns FALSE with errno = EINVAL when the day of month is 1 and the hour is 0 (first hour of the first day of a month); that case is handled by the code, not a precondition. Otherwise it sets the calendar to the first day, 00:00:00 of the month containing now64 (starttime) and to the same time one month later via month++ (ttime), builds a leap_info_t with ttime, stime = low 32 bits of ttime - starttime, taiof = (newest entry's taiof if the table has entries, else head.base_tai) + 1 when insert is nonzero or - 1 when it is zero, and dynls = 1, and returns add_range(pt, &li). add_range (read at 725-767) shifts the entries down and inserts the new one at index 0 (dropping the oldest when the table is full), invalidates cached limits through reset_times, and returns TRUE; it does not set errno. No locks.

name: loop_config
prose: loop_config(item, freq), ntp_loopfilter.c:1256-1398, returns void and switches on item. LOOP_DRIFTINIT does nothing when LOCKCLOCK is defined; otherwise, with KERNEL_PLL, it breaks out immediately if mode_ntpdate is set (skipping everything below, including set_freq, rstclock and loop_started), else calls start_kern_loop() first; then it clamps init_drift_comp/1e6 to the range -NTP_MAXFREQ..NTP_MAXFREQ, calls set_freq on it, calls rstclock(EVNT_FSET, 0) if freq_set is nonzero or rstclock(EVNT_NSET, 0) otherwise, and sets loop_started = TRUE. LOOP_KERN_CLEAR does nothing (its body is under #if 0). LOOP_ALLAN stores (u_char)freq in allan_xpt; LOOP_CODEC stores freq/1e6 in clock_codec; LOOP_PHI stores freq/1e6 in clock_phi; LOOP_FREQ stores init_drift_comp = freq and freq_set = 1; LOOP_NOFREQ sets both to 0; LOOP_PANIC stores clock_panic; LOOP_MINSTEP stores max(freq, CLOCK_MINSTEP) in clock_minstep; LOOP_TICK calls set_sys_tick_precision(freq). LOOP_HUFFPUFF raises freq to at least HUFFPUFF, sets sys_hufflen = (int)(freq / HUFFPUFF), allocates sys_huffpuff with eallocarray (the previous array is not freed here), fills it with 1e9 and sets sys_mindly = 1e9. LOOP_MAX sets both clock_max_fwd and clock_max_back to freq; LOOP_MAX_BACK sets clock_max_back and LOOP_MAX_FWD sets clock_max_fwd; in the three cases select_loop(FALSE) is called when freq is 0 or above 0.5 (LOOP_MAX), or, for the two single-direction cases, when either clock_max_back or clock_max_fwd is 0 or above 0.5. LOOP_LEAP and any other value log "loop_config: unsupported option %d" at LOG_NOTICE. No locks are taken.

name: local_clock
prose: local_clock(peer, fp_offset), ntp_loopfilter.c:452-933, applies a new clock offset to the discipline loop and returns an int. It returns 0 after only calling record_loop_stats if ntp_enable is false. It returns -1 (after report_event EVNT_SYSFAULT) when |fp_offset| exceeds clock_panic, clock_panic > 0 and allow_panic is not set; otherwise allow_panic is cleared. In mode_ntpdate it steps (step_systime) when the offset exceeds the forward/backward step threshold, else slews (adj_systime), logs, records stats and calls exit(0), so it does not return. With a huff-n-puff table it adjusts fp_offset by half the delay excess. It then clamps sys_poll to the peer's minpoll..maxpoll, computes mu = current_time - clock_epoch and sets rval = 1. If the offset exceeds clock_max_fwd or clock_max_back (when those are > 0) or force_step_once is set, it switches on state: EVNT_SYNC reports EVNT_SPIK, sets state = EVNT_SPIK and returns 0; EVNT_FREQ returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise computes direct_freq and goes on to the SPIK case; EVNT_SPIK returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise falls to the default case; the default case (also NSET and FSET) reports EVNT_CLOCKRESET, steps the clock, reinits the timer, sets tc_counter = 0, clock_jitter to the precision, sets rval = 2, and if the state was EVNT_NSET calls rstclock(EVNT_FREQ, 0) and returns 2 at once, otherwise calls rstclock(EVNT_SYNC, 0) and continues. Early returns of 0 happen without calling record_loop_stats. If the offset is inside the step threshold, it updates clock_jitter and by state: EVNT_NSET slews with adj_systime and calls rstclock(EVNT_FREQ, fp_offset); EVNT_FREQ returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise computes direct_freq and falls through (as the default path); default (including SYNC and FSET) adjusts clock_frequency (Allan/PLL terms when freq_cnt == 0) and calls rstclock(EVNT_SYNC, fp_offset), resetting freq_cnt if |fp_offset| < CLOCK_FLOOR. Both non-returning paths then, if the kernel loop is enabled and freq_cnt == 0, build an ntp_adjtime request (offset, constant, status, leap flags, PPS flags), call it, and read back clock_offset and clock_frequency, setting loop_tai if changed. Finally it logs if |clock_frequency| exceeds NTP_MAXFREQ, stores drift_comp clamped to +/-NTP_MAXFREQ, updates clock_stability and the tc_counter/sys_poll hysteresis (calling poll_update if sys_poll changed), calls record_loop_stats and returns rval, which is 2 after a step and 1 otherwise.

name: receive
prose: receive(rbufp), ntp_proto.c:626-2553, is the NTP packet input routine; it returns void and most outcomes are early returns. It increments sys_received first (line 686, before any return) and looks up the restriction mask. It then drops the packet, each time with a different counter, as follows: sys_badlength for a bogus port or length, an old-version or invalid-mode or invalid-poll packet, or a bad length at several MAC/extension-length checks; sys_restricted for RES_IGNORE, private (mode 7) packets without ntp_mode7 or with RES_NOQUERY, control packets with RES_NOQUERY, RES_DONTSERVE, RES_FLAKE, RES_DONTTRUST with no MAC, and for several later access-denied cases; sys_limitrejected when RES_LIMITED is set and the rate is exceeded (the code at 957-977 returns in that case, depending on KOD handling); sys_declined in several association-setup cases; sys_badauth in an autokey MAC-length failure and at a later authentication failure. Control and private packets are handed to process_control or process_private and the function returns. sys_newversion or sys_oldversion is incremented for packets passing the version test. A crypto-NAK that is invalid (valid_NAK returns INVALIDNAK) calls report_event, increments peer->badNAK when peer is non-NULL, logs, and returns without incrementing any sys_* counter (lines 1039-1046). A packet without a MAC is not dropped by authentication: it is accepted with is_authentic = AUTH_NONE (and RES_MSSNTP cleared); a valid crypto-NAK gets AUTH_CRYPTO; otherwise the MAC is checked with authdecrypt giving AUTH_OK or AUTH_ERROR. An existing peer whose keyid differs from the packet's key id, or whose MAC fails authentication, is dropped with sys_restricted. The function then dispatches on the association match code (fast_xmit replies for AM_FXMIT, newpeer creation for manycast/broadcast-client/passive cases, several sys_declined or sys_restricted drops, and AM_PROCPKT/AM_ERR handling). For an existing peer it increments peer->received, does the on-wire/timestamp checks (bogus or old packets return after incrementing peer->bogusorg or peer->oldpkt), kiss-o'-death handling, authentication-failure handling (peer->badauth), autokey checks via crypto_recv, and finally calls process_packet(peer, pkt, rbufp->recv_length) and, if the packet tests pass, poll_update and the nextdate adjustment for flipped peers.

name: check_leapsec
prose: Static function check_leapsec(now, tpiv, reset), ntp_timer.c:550-732, returns void. It first calls leapsec_electric(pll_control && kern_enable) (or leapsec_electric(0) without KERNEL_PLL; not under SYS_WINNT), and sets leap_smear.enabled under LEAP_SMEAR. If reset is nonzero it sets lsprox = LSPROX_NOWARN, calls leapsec_reset_frame and zeroes lsdata; sys_tai is not changed on this path. Otherwise it calls leapsec_query(&lsdata, now, tpiv). If the query reports a full hit (fired) it computes the clock warp: for a negative warp it steps the clock (step_systime) only when clock_max_back > 0 and smaller than the warp magnitude, otherwise only logs a slew message; for a positive warp likewise against clock_max_fwd; it logs the chosen message, calls report_event(EVNT_LEAP), sets lsprox and the global leapsec to LSPROX_NOWARN and sys_tai to lsdata.tai_offs. If not fired it sets lsprox = lsdata.proximity and sys_tai = lsdata.tai_offs (noting a change of sys_tai for autokey). With LEAP_SMEAR it also maintains the smear interval and offset. Then, unless the red-alert guard blocks it ((leapsec > 0 or lsprox < LSPROX_ALERT) and leapsec < lsprox), a rise of the proximity level sets leapsec = lsprox, reporting PEVNT_ARMED with sys_peer when lsdata.dynamic or EVNT_ARMED otherwise, only when the level crosses from below LSPROX_SCHEDULE to at or above it; a fall of the level (leapsec > lsprox) reports EVNT_DISARMED when crossing below LSPROX_SCHEDULE and sets leapsec = lsprox. It then sets leapdif = lsdata.tai_diff when leapsec >= LSPROX_SCHEDULE, else 0, calls check_leap_sec_in_progress(&lsdata) (which recomputes leap_sec_in_progress and calls set_sys_leap(sys_leap) when it changed), and under AUTOKEY calls crypto_update_taichange() if sys_tai changed or the leap fired.

name: simulate_server
prose: int simulate_server(serv_addr, inter, rpkt), ntpsim.c:255-377, is the simulator's server model, called with the client request rpkt. It zeroes a reply packet and receive buffer, scans simulation.servers[0..num_of_servers-1] and takes the first entry whose addr memcmp-equals *serv_addr (so with duplicates the first one wins), prints a "Received packet" line to stderr, and calls abortsim("Server with specified address not found!!!") if none matched; it relies on abortsim (defined outside this file, not read) not returning, since server->curr_script is dereferenced straight after at line 293, and curr_script is never checked for NULL. It builds a stratum-1 reply with refid "GPS", ppoll/precision copied from the request, org = the request's xmt, and delays d1, d3 = poisson(curr_script->prop_delay, curr_script->jitter), d2 = poisson(curr_script->proc_delay, 0); t1 is the request transmit time, t2 = server->server_time + d1, t3 = t2 + d2 (stored as rec and xmt), t4 = t1 + d1 + d2 + d3. It fills a recvbuf (receiver = receive, length LEN_PKT_NOMAC, dstadr = inter, source address copied from *serv_addr), creates a PACKET event at t4 with event(t4, PACKET), copies the buffer into it and enqueues it on event_queue. If curr_script->duration > simulation.sim_time and HEAD_PFIFO(server->script) is NULL it prints "Hello" and unlinks curr_script from the server's script FIFO (no free). It then returns 0; the only way out other than the abortsim path is this return 0.

name: teljjy_conn_send
prose: Static function teljjy_conn_send(peer, pp, up), refclock_jjy.c:3346-3440, sends the next command of the TELJJY command sequence and returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE or TELJJY_STAY_CLOCK_STATE. Otherwise, for sequence 0 with peer->ttl == 100 it sets iClockCommandSeq to TELJJY_COMMAND_START_SKIP_LOOPBACK; for sequence 0 with ttl != 100 it resets iLoopbackCount and clears bLoopbackTimeout[]; for sequence > 0 with ttl != 100, a current entry whose expected reply type is TELJJY_REPLY_LOOPBACK and iLoopbackCount < MAX_LOOPBACK it calls teljjy_setDelay and increments iLoopbackCount. It then increments iClockCommandSeq and reads the new entry's command and length. If that command is NULL it returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE (nothing written). Otherwise it write()s the command to pp->io.fd, calling refclock_report(CEVNT_FAULT) if the byte count differs from the length (it still carries on); for a loopback-type command it records the send time in sendTime[iLoopbackCount] and sets bLoopbackMode when iLoopbackCount < MAX_LOOPBACK, else logs a bug message and clears bLoopbackMode; for other commands it clears bLoopbackMode. name: wwv_endpoc
prose: Static function wwv_endpoc(peer, epopos), refclock_wwv.c:1382-1593, is called once per second with the second-comb-filter epoch maximum position and returns void; it keeps its state in function statics (median filter, scount, syncnt, maxrun, zepoch, zcount, avgcnt, avginc and so on) and in the wwvunit. It increments scount, then if up->epomax < STHR or up->eposnr < SSNR it clears the SSYNC and FGATE status bits, sets avgcnt, syncnt and maxrun to 0 and returns. If neither SELV nor SELH is set it returns with nothing else changed (scount was already incremented). Otherwise it pushes epopos through a 3-entry median filter to get tepoch, computes tmp2 = (tepoch - xepoch) % WWV_SEC; when tmp2 is 0 it increments syncnt and, if syncnt > SCMP, MSYNC is set and (FGATE is set or scount - zcount <= up->avgint), it sets SSYNC and up->yepoch = tepoch; when tmp2 is nonzero and syncnt >= maxrun it records the run (maxrun, mcount, mepoch) and clears syncnt. With CLK_FLAG4 and no MSYNC it writes a clockstats line. It increments avgcnt and, if avgcnt < up->avgint, saves xepoch = tepoch and returns (so no frequency or interval adjustment on that call, even though SSYNC and yepoch may already have been set above). At the end of the averaging interval it updates the longest run, sets xepoch, and computes dtemp = (mepoch - zepoch) % WWV_SEC; if FGATE is set and |dtemp| < MAXFREQ*MINAVG it adjusts up->freq (clamped to +/-MAXFREQ) and, when |dtemp| < MAXFREQ*MINAVG/2, moves the avginc ratchet up and doubles up->avgint (if below MAXAVG) after avginc reaches 3; if FGATE is set and |dtemp| is larger, it moves the ratchet down and halves up->avgint (if above MINAVG) after avginc reaches -3, so avgint can be reduced in that case. It then optionally writes clockstats, sets FGATE, saves zepoch = mepoch and zcount = mcount, and resets avgcnt, syncnt and maxrun to 0. When FGATE was not set the freq and avgint adjustment block is skipped.

name: wwvb_receive
prose: Static function wwvb_receive(rbufp), refclock_wwvb.c:247-443, returns void. It reads a line with refclock_gtlin(rbufp, pp->a_lastcode, BMAX, &trtmp). If that returns 0 (empty line) it stores trtmp in up->laststamp only when up->prev_eol_cr was false, toggles up->prev_eol_cr, and returns. Otherwise it sets pp->lencode to the length, pp->lastrec to the old up->laststamp, up->laststamp to trtmp and up->prev_eol_cr to TRUE, and returns if pp->lastrec is zero. It then initialises the sync, quality, leap and dst characters to ' ' and parses a_lastcode by pp->lencode: LENWWVB0 and LENWWVB2 and LENWWVB3 each use a sscanf format (format 0: sync, day, hour, minute, second, dst, tz, 8 fields, nsec = 0; format 2: sync, quality, year, day, h:m:s.msec, leap, 9 fields, nsec = msec * 1e6; format 3: sync, year, month, day, h/m/s, dst, leap, 8 fields, day from ymd2yd, nsec = 0). A short sscanf or any other length goes to the bad-format path: when up->linect > 0 it decrements linect and records the line in clockstats, otherwise it reports CEVNT_BADREPLY, then returns. After a successful parse it sets pp->disp from the quality character (' ' gives .001 and also sets pp->lastref = pp->lastrec; 'A' .01; 'B' .1; 'C' .5; 'D' MAXDISPERSE; any other character gives MAXDISPERSE and reports CEVNT_BADREPLY), and sets pp->leap to LEAP_NOTINSYNC if the sync character is not ' ', else LEAP_ADDSECOND if the leap character is 'L', else LEAP_NOWARNING. Under HAVE_PPSAPI it increments up->tcount and returns if the peer has FLAG_PPS. Otherwise it calls refclock_process_f(pp, pp->fudgetime2) and reports CEVNT_BADTIME if that returns false. Formats 0 and 3 leave the quality character at ' ', so they take the ' ' branch.

name: ntpqmain
prose: ntpqmain(argc, argv), ntpq.c:502-657 (compiled unless BUILD_AS_LIB), is the body of the ntpq program; the wrapper main at ntpq.c:490-497 (built unless NO_MAIN_ALLOWED) just returns ntpqmain(argc, argv), but the code in this slice is ntpqmain itself. It turns interactive mode on when there are no command-line commands (defcmds == 0) and both stdin and stderr are terminals. It installs the ctrl-C hook (and push_ctrl_c_handler(abortcmd) when interactive). If command-line commands were given (numcmds > 0) it opens each host with openhost and, for each host that opened, runs each command with docmd (printing blank-line separators), then frees the command strings. If defcmds == 0 it opens the first host (ignoring the result) and runs getcmds() for the interactive loop. It then returns 0; the ntpq-specific functions it calls may exit the process themselves, which was not checked.

name: arc4random_uniform
prose: arc4random_uniform(upper_bound), arc4random.c:512-545 (compiled unless ARC4RANDOM_NOUNIFORM), returns an unsigned int below upper_bound. It returns 0 at once, without calling the generator, if upper_bound < 2. Otherwise it computes min = 2^32 mod upper_bound: when unsigned int is wider than 32 bits (UINT_MAX > 0xffffffffUL) as 0x100000000UL % upper_bound; otherwise, avoiding 64-bit math, as 1 + ~upper_bound for upper_bound > 0x80000000 and ((0xffffffff - upper_bound*2) + 1) % upper_bound for smaller values. It then loops, calling arc4random() until a draw r >= min (the loop has no iteration limit in the code), and returns r % upper_bound. The result is less than upper_bound; it is uniform over that range to the extent that arc4random() is uniform over 32 bits. Each arc4random() call advances the shared generator state (and may reseed), so the function is not free of global-state effects.

name: evbuffer_read
prose: evbuffer_read(buf, fd, howmuch), buffer.c:2283-2412, reads from fd into the evbuffer and returns an int. It takes the buffer lock with EVBUFFER_LOCK (a no-op when the buffer has no lock) and releases it at the done label on every return. It returns -1 immediately if buf->freeze_end is set. Otherwise it asks get_n_bytes_readable_on_socket (FIONREAD, or EVBUFFER_MAX_READ when unavailable), uses EVBUFFER_MAX_READ if that is <= 0 or above the maximum, and sets howmuch to that value if howmuch is negative or larger. It then makes room: with iovecs via evbuffer_expand_fast_ (return -1 on failure) and readv/WSARecv into the chain space, or without iovecs via evbuffer_expand_singlechain (return -1 on NULL) and read/recv into that chain. This expansion can allocate or add chains before the read, so on the following -1 or 0 returns the buffer contents and total_len are unchanged but its capacity may have grown. If the read returns -1 (or WSARecv fails with an error other than WSAECONNABORTED) the result is -1; a return of 0 (or WSAECONNABORTED) gives 0, with no change to total_len or callbacks. For n > 0 it advances the chain offsets (and last_with_datap) by n, adds n to total_len and n_add_for_cb, calls evbuffer_invoke_callbacks_ and returns n.

name: evbuffer_run_callbacks
prose: Static function evbuffer_run_callbacks(buffer, running_deferred), buffer.c:455-511, returns void; the caller must hold the buffer lock (ASSERT_EVBUFFER_LOCKED at line 478). It chooses a flag mask and a pending-counter policy: when running_deferred is nonzero it runs callbacks that have EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED set and EVBUFFER_CB_NODEFER clear (the deferred ones) and clears the counters; when running_deferred is zero and buffer->deferred_cbs is set it runs only callbacks with both ENABLED and NODEFER set and does not clear n_add_for_cb and n_del_for_cb; otherwise it runs every ENABLED callback (NODEFER not examined) and clears the counters. If the callback list is empty it sets both counters to 0 and returns (also when deferral is on). If both counters are already 0 it returns with no callbacks run. Otherwise it fills a cb_info with total_len, the added and deleted counts and orig_size = total_len + n_del_for_cb - n_add_for_cb, clears the counters when the policy says to, and for each entry matching the mask calls the obsolete-style callback (EVBUFFER_CB_OBSOLETE, with orig_size and new size) or the normal callback with the info; the next pointer is read before each call.
